Korean firms are already using UN-issued Article 6/PACM credits (e.g. a Myanmar cookstove project) for K-ETS compliance. No ITMO issuance or transfer specifically involving Korea has been confirmed (see ITMO Transfer Status).

A peer-reviewed modeling study estimated Korea's tidal flats hold ~11.2 million MgC (~41.3M tCO2e, to 70cm depth) and projected a 2050 contribution of ~7.64M tCO2e/year toward Korea's carbon-neutral strategy — the study's authors describe this as relevant for future NDC inclusion, though it is not yet formally counted in Korea's NDC.

notes: Japan's GX-ETS ran as a voluntary baseline-and-credit scheme through FY2023–FY2025, then became mandatory from FY2026, covering roughly 60% of national emissions (~600 MtCO2e) with a price band (FY2026: ¥1,700 floor / ¥4,300 ceiling, rising 3%/yr); auctioning phases in from FY2033. In April 2025 the JCM Promotion and Utilization Council formally authorized the JCM as an Article 6.2 cooperative approach. As of mid-2025, Japan was reportedly considering barring international voluntary-market credits from GX-ETS compliance as the mandatory phase approached — not confirmed finalized as of this update.

notes: The Climate Change (Carbon Markets) Regulations, 2024 were gazetted in May 2024, establishing Kenya's Designated National Authority (DNA) and its role approving carbon projects. Kenya's National Carbon Registry launched 17 Feb 2026 to centralize registration, track emission reductions, and authorize transfers. An Aug 2026 rulebook set Kenya's Article 6 international-transfer budget at 10M tCO2e through 2030 (annual allocations capped at 1.67M tCO2e), covering energy, transport, industrial processes and waste. article6_framework and domestic_carbon_market upgraded from "In Development" to "Implemented" on this basis — both DNA and registry are now live, operational institutions, not just a published framework. No specific project authorization or bilateral partner agreement has been confirmed yet, so article6_authorization and bilateral_agreements remain "In Development". An earlier legal analysis (pre-registry) also noted the 2024 regulations didn't fully define carbon credits' legal status or synchronization with international voluntary-market trading — unclear whether the Aug 2026 rulebook closed that gap.

notes: Mexico's domestic ETS (launched 2020, pilot 2020–2021, transitional phase 2022–2025) targets an "Operational Phase" around late 2025/early 2026, covering ~40% of national GHG emissions from large industrial/energy installations. The RMX (Mexican Registry for the Green Transition) offset standard is meant to supply ETS demand, but is explicitly separate from the national infrastructure Article 6/CORSIA authorization would require — which still doesn't exist. One analysis warns the ETS's own offset rules may complicate future Article 6.2/6.4 deals.
